title: Skyline-Preserving Building Height Optimization
description:
You are given an n × n matrix representing a city where grid[r][c] is the height of the building at that position. The city's skyline consists of the maximum building heights when viewed from the four cardinal directions (North, South, East, West). Specifically, the West and East skylines are determined by the maximum height in each row, while the North and South skylines are determined by the maximum height in each column.

You can increase the height of any building by any amount (starting from height 0), provided that the skyline from all four directions remains exactly the same. Your task is to calculate the maximum total increase in building heights possible without altering the skyline.
input_format:
The first line contains two integers n and n (number of rows and columns, which are always equal).
The next n lines each contain n space-separated integers representing the grid heights.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the maximum total increase in height possible.
